prose:
Historian Mark Humphries describes a prerelease GPT-6.2 Astra session identifying the vicomte de Chabot as a candidate creator of an anonymous 1808 sketchbook. A diary clue led to a paper travel journal, and the author reports that later examination of archival copies supported the attribution. The account includes the model's search process and the historian's interpretation.

The twenty-two-minute model investigation is separate from later receipt and reading of archival copies; the archive and attribution were not independently audited here. This is the fuller source behind [Willison's earlier link post](../summaries/920d51a93807.md), not an independent replication. The essay's broad mathematical and intelligence-explosion framing does not verify unrelated proof claims or establish that historical research is solved generally.
highlights: Case begins with a specific anonymous sketchbook
Model proposes a named creator and an archival check
Twenty-two minutes covers the model's lead-finding phase
Human archival work supplies later reported support
This is the source of the earlier secondary link post
No independent archive audit or historical benchmark was performed
Unrelated mathematical claims retain their separate status
Author compares handwriting, itinerary and a matching sketch entry
